subject: Agriculture
title: Rinderpest Eradication
description: A micro-lesson that makes Rinderpest Eradication usable.

hook.text: Rinderpest killed cattle by the millions for centuries. In 2011, it became only the second disease ever eradicated.

buildup.text: The virus caused fever, diarrhea, and death in cattle—sometimes killing 90% of herds in an outbreak.

discovery.text: Walter Plowright developed a heat-stable vaccine in the 1960s that worked in tropical conditions.

twist.text: The final push required vaccinating cattle in war zones—Somalia, Afghanistan, even during active conflicts.

climax.text: Rinderpest joined smallpox as the only diseases completely eliminated from the planet. A veterinary triumph.

punchline.text: We wiped out a disease. Only the second time in history.

quiz.question: What distinction does rinderpest hold in disease history?
options: Only the second disease ever eradicated, after smallpox

details.summary: Rinderpest was a devastating viral cattle plague that killed millions of animals for centuries until a global vaccination campaign eradicated it in 2011. This topic covers the disease's impact, the eradication effort, and its significance as only the second disease ever eradicated.
details.whyItMatters: Rinderpest is only the second disease eradicated in history after smallpox. Its elimination saved millions of livestock lives annually and demonstrated that global veterinary cooperation can defeat devastating animal diseases.
takeaways: Rinderpest killed up to 90% of cattle herds in affected regions and devastated pastoral communities
A heat-stable vaccine developed in the 1980s enabled vaccination in remote tropical areas
Rinderpest was declared eradicated in 2011—only the second disease ever eliminated

faq.question: What was rinderpest and why was it so devastating?
faq.answer: Rinderpest was a highly contagious viral disease of cattle and other ruminants that caused fever, mouth ulcers, diarrhea, and death in up to 90% of infected animals. Outbreaks caused famines by killing the animals that communities depended on for food and labor.

faq.question: How was rinderpest eradicated?
faq.answer: A decades-long global campaign combined mass vaccination with surveillance, outbreak response, and community engagement. The development of a thermostable vaccine that did not require cold storage was the breakthrough enabling vaccination in remote tropical regions.
